name: – David McAllister – § 50 – Am 50
title: REPORT on the implementation of the common foreign and security policy – 2024 annual report
part_text: 50. Takes note of the ongoing escalation in trade relations between the United States and the EU; expresses its concern that a trade war has the potential to significantly harm many export-dependent sectors of the economies of the Member States, and in particular affect workers and SMEs ; calls for the swift implementation of proportionate countermeasures in response to the tariffs already imposed and soon to be imposed on EU goods imported into the United States, calls on the Commission and the Council to consider triggering the EU’s anti-coercion instrument if necessary, calls on the Member States to set up aid programmes and funds to support the workers and SMEs in the sectors most affected by the consequences of the trade measures; underlines that the EU’s vulnerability to sudden changes in US trade policy is the by-product of decades of trade liberalisation ; believes that, in the longer term, it is necessary to reduce the exposure of the EU and its Member States to unilateral trade policy changes in third countries, emphasises that this implies a complete overhaul of EU trade policy, a rebalancing of economies and a transformation of production in order to reverse over-specialisation in some specific sectors and to prioritise domestic needs rather than competitiveness and promotion of exports;
